title: New Robot Butler Can Help You Find Your Keys
paragraphs: Have you ever wasted time searching for your keys or your phone? A company in the United States is developing a home robot that may one day help you find them.

The robot, called Voxel Series-1, is being developed by Tuesday Labs, a robotics company in New York. It is a humanoid robot that walks on two legs. Its knees bend backward, and its legs can change its height, so it can get close to furniture and shelves. It also has two arms and hands that can grab, hold, pull and release objects.

Voxel has several cameras that help it see its surroundings. The company plans for the robot to scan homes continuously and use machine learning to learn the layout of each home and where things belong. This would allow it to remember where people leave their belongings.

According to Tuesday Labs, Voxel is designed to tidy messy rooms, find lost items and bring things to people when they ask. It could also water plants and do other repetitive household chores. In the future, it might also help with jobs such as laundry and washing dishes. The robot is also designed to walk very quietly and stay steady on uneven ground.

However, people who want a robot butler will need to be patient and have a lot of money. Voxel is expected to cost about $20,000. People can reserve one for $200, but production is not expected to start until 2028. The robot's full abilities are also still being developed.
Experts say that it has not yet been shown that the robot can reliably do a wide range of household chores. Other home robots have also promised a lot in the past.
Some people may also have concerns about privacy, because the robot would continuously scan their homes.
